cases.name: Libra Internet Bank
cases.headline: 35% less test-creation time
cases.finding: UiPath reports 35% less time creating test cases and AI generation for more than 60% of cases used. The pilot began with two onboarding teams.
cases.change: Requirements in Jira feed AI-generated cases alongside Xray and Test Manager; smoke automation expanded separately.
cases.limit: Vendor-published customer account. Sample, measurement window and net review effort are undisclosed. The 90%+ smoke automation figure applies to teams using UiPath.
cases.lesson: Try reviewed scenario drafting on one onboarding journey; measure accepted coverage and total effort.

cases.name: Goldman Sachs
cases.headline: 36% → 72% coverage
cases.unit: Reported unit-test coverage for a selected module
cases.finding: Diffblue reports this coverage increase within 24 hours. A separate application received 3,211 generated tests; review took one day.
cases.change: AI-based Java regression-test generation supports legacy modernization.
cases.limit: Vendor case. Manual-time savings use assumed 30 minutes per test and six productive hours per day. Coverage records exercised code, not proven business correctness; this is not an LLM rollout benchmark.
cases.lesson: Generate candidates in a buildable module, then challenge assertions against independently specified behavior.

cases.name: DBS
cases.headline: 5% → 100% of changes screened
cases.finding: DBS reports an 81% decrease in monthly average change-related incidents with AI risk scoring. It separately describes JIRA Assist for user stories and test cases.
cases.change: Near-production testing, stronger change practices and ML-based screening support delivery reliability.
cases.limit: Bank self-report, without a causal control or raw incident counts. The incident result belongs to change-risk management; no JIRA Assist productivity percentage is reported.
cases.lesson: Evaluate change-risk suggestions against known outcomes before allowing them to alter mandatory testing.

cases.name: Fiserv
cases.headline: 65% fewer major incidents
cases.finding: Tricentis reports the decline during testing standardization across a large application estate.
cases.change: A testing centre of excellence connects Jira, qTest, Tosca and data validation, with shared training.
cases.limit: Vendor case with multiple simultaneous changes. AI testing is a subsequent pilot; the quoted 25% AI uplift is an expectation, not a measured result.
cases.lesson: Establish shared evidence, framework ownership and reusable data checks while piloting AI.

cases.name: Bank of Queensland
cases.headline: 5+ weeks → 5 days
cases.finding: The case reports shorter regression cycles within an 18-month transformation and releases moving from every three to four months to monthly.
cases.change: Tosca and qTest support existing testers, traceability and daily environment health checks.
cases.limit: Vendor modernization case. Service virtualization and Vision AI appear as future work; the reported cycle reduction cannot be assigned to them.
cases.lesson: Remove environment waits and build usable automation before promising a shorter release cycle.

cases.name: ANZ
cases.headline: 30.98 → 17.86 minutes
cases.unit: Mean self-reported time per Python challenge
cases.finding: The controlled crossover study involved over 100 engineers. Analysis retained 172 task observations after removing six duplicates and 22 unsolved tasks.
cases.change: Copilot access switched between groups; participants attempted fixed Python problems.
cases.limit: Coding experiment, not QE delivery. Time was self-reported; failed tasks were excluded. The time test used 22 paired participants; unit-test success improvement was not statistically significant.
cases.lesson: Compare matched tasks, retain unsuccessful attempts and measure quality separately from speed.

cases.name: Unnamed fintech software provider
cases.headline: 42% less QA cycle effort claimed
cases.finding: TestingXperts reports AI use in test design, automation, impact analysis, reporting and investigation.
cases.change: Several workflow interventions are bundled in one engagement.
cases.limit: Client, sample and measurement period are undisclosed. The separate 60–70% productivity claim is not reconciled with its 10-hour to 4–5-hour example. Seek definitions and raw data before quoting it as a benchmark.
cases.lesson: Use the workflow ideas to frame discovery; exclude the headline from the client savings forecast.

practices.title: Start with a bounded journey
practices.body: Choose one onboarding or payment change with clear expected outcomes. Preserve the current toolchain where it supports the trial.
practices.proof: A domain reviewer can accept or reject each proposed scenario.

practices.title: Give tests an independent correctness check
practices.body: Coverage and passing tests are useful signals. Challenge money movement, rounding and retries with known failures and reviewed expected outcomes.
practices.proof: A duplicate transfer or wrong balance causes the candidate test to fail.

practices.title: Modernize the execution foundation
practices.body: Assign owners to environments, fixture reset, dependency models and reusable frameworks. Track their improvements separately from AI.
practices.proof: Another engineer reproduces the run and locates its original evidence.

practices.title: Keep the comparison honest
practices.body: Use comparable work, the same readiness level and explicit task allocation. Include failures, review, rework and setup; record missing observations.
practices.proof: The team can explain selection, exclusions and uncertainty in the result.

practices.title: Run recommendations beside the existing process
practices.body: Observe risk-based test selection or triage suggestions before changing required suites. Inspect missed defects and incorrect groupings.
practices.proof: Mandatory payment checks still run, and wrong suggestions are visible.

practices.title: Scale a supported service
practices.body: Coach domain QA and automation engineers together. Name a support owner and test transfer to a second team before expanding across 50–100 staff.
practices.proof: The second team uses and maintains the pattern without its original authors.

pilots.title: Onboarding test design
pilots.fit: Manual case writing dominates; requirements and domain reviewers are available.
pilots.stack: Jira + Xray, or Azure Boards + Test Plans; an approved assistant drafts into the existing review workflow.
pilots.input: One onboarding journey, approved acceptance rules, historic cases and known omissions.
pilots.output: A reviewed scenario matrix, rejected drafts and traceable expected outcomes.
pilots.dependency: Approved source access, consistent requirements, reviewer time and a conventional-work baseline.
pilots.measure: Active minutes per accepted scenario, review/rework, missed critical cases and duplicate cases.
pilots.gate: All required onboarding rules are covered and independently reviewed; net effort improves on comparable work.
pilots.fail: Pause if reviewers cannot establish correctness or critical scenarios are omitted.
pilots.question: Which onboarding rule is repeatedly missed, and who can judge a proposed test against it?
pilots.modernization: QE modernization for this scope: versioned requirements, a curated scenario catalog, independent expected outcomes and a named domain reviewer. Reviewed drafting may start while execution foundations are improved; generated execution waits for its own prerequisites.

pilots.title: Payment API test generation
pilots.fit: A buildable service, stable API tests and repeatable test data already exist.
pilots.stack: JUnit + REST Assured; Testcontainers or a supported environment; WireMock at the provider boundary; existing CI.
pilots.input: PAY-142 rules, repository conventions, synthetic accounts and provider scenarios.
pilots.output: A reviewed test pull request, deliberate-fault results and retained CI artifacts.
pilots.dependency: Build access, permitted AI tooling, runtime capacity, isolated fixtures, owned stubs and independent financial assertions.
pilots.measure: Effort per accepted change, assertion strength, flaky failures, setup time and repeatability.
pilots.gate: Required checks pass on the intended build and fail on a deliberately broken duplicate-posting variant.
pilots.fail: Stop if a candidate weakens assertions, silently skips required checks or passes the broken variant.
pilots.question: Can two engineers reproduce the same payment failure in an isolated environment today?
pilots.modernization: QE modernization for this scope: a maintained unit/API suite, independent financial assertions, resettable synthetic data, repeatable environments, controlled provider behavior and retained CI evidence. Use containers where suitable or a supported reproducible alternative; validate virtual services against contracts and separate real integration.

pilots.title: Failure triage and evidence
pilots.fit: Test runs already retain usable logs, traces, assertions and defect dispositions.
pilots.stack: Existing CI and test management; Playwright traces or API logs; approved AI summaries linked to source artifacts.
pilots.input: A bounded set of historical failures with independently adjudicated causes, then new failures in shadow mode.
pilots.output: Evidence-linked draft diagnoses with uncertainty, reviewer corrections and original run links.
pilots.dependency: Accessible diagnostics, run IDs, reviewer capacity and a policy for retaining permitted evidence.
pilots.measure: Time to correct disposition, unsupported claims, wrong grouping, missed product defects and review burden.
pilots.gate: Reviewers can trace every material claim to evidence, and product defects remain visible.
pilots.fail: Pause if the tool invents a cause, hides an unresolved failure or collapses distinct product defects.
pilots.question: How much time is spent finding evidence versus making the actual diagnosis?
pilots.modernization: QE modernization for this scope: reliable test outcomes, stable run IDs, retained logs/traces, known defect dispositions and named owners for tests, data and environments. Recommendations stay in shadow mode until their accuracy is reviewed; missing diagnostics require remediation first. This diagnostic-only trial does not execute fixes or retests; assess Triage & retest separately before expanding its scope.

flow.title: Approved intent reaches the assistant
flow.detail: The domain owner supplies expected behavior and permitted context.

flow.title: A candidate reaches review
flow.detail: Generated tests remain proposals. A reviewer checks their intent and assertions.

flow.title: Reviewed tests face an independent challenge
flow.detail: CI runs the normal build and a known-bad variant against controlled fixtures.

flow.title: Invalid candidates return for correction
flow.detail: A compile error, wrong assertion or failure to detect the known fault rejects the candidate. Nothing is promoted.
